newsitem.title: UK: Ibca says assigns Russian bank Unexim long-term BB.
newsitem.headline: Ibca says assigns Russian bank Unexim long-term BB.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said on Monday it had assigned the Russian bank Unexim (United Export Import Bank) with long-term BB, short-term B, individual C/D and legal 2T ratings.

LONDON, June 2 -- IBCA, the European credit rating agency, has assigned the following ratings to the major Russian bank Unexim (United Export Import Bank): Long-term BB, Short-term B, Individual C/D and Legal 2T. This is the first 2T Legal rating that IBCA has so far given for any Russian bank, and reflects Unexim's importance in the banking community and economy, as well as its size and connections with the government. Unexim has a special place in the Russian banking system, being one of the major lenders to the Russian government, regional administrations and several major industrial companies. It is currently involved in attempting to ease the payment crisis in Russian industry where companies are often unable to pay neither each other nor their taxes, thereby creating budgetary problems for the Russian government.
The bank is also involved in promissory note schemes issued to companies, most of which are guaranteed by the Ministry of Finance.

IBCA notes that asset quality has been acceptable compared with many Russian banks', probably reflecting Unexim's concentration on larger companies, although the payment crisis and arrears makes the solvency of Russian corporates difficult to determine.

The bank is accredited to the EBRD's/World Bank's FIDP Programme, has credit lines from international lenders, has received SEC recognition for custody services, and has opened a Swiss subsidiary, Banque Unixem (Suisse) SA.
At end-1996, the capital ratio, calculated in accordance with Basle G10 requirements, was 13% and a share issue of USD100 million is planned for 1997.
